title: Review all major FBI investigations and end improper ones
proposal: The chapter says the next Administration should immediately review all major active FBI investigations and activities and end any that are unlawful or against the national interest, possibly publishing a report.
quote: Conduct an immediate, comprehensive review of all major active FBI investigations and activities and terminate any that are unlawful or contrary to the national interest.

title: Place the FBI under DOJ's criminal and national security chiefs
proposal: The chapter says the Attorney General should move the FBI out from direct supervision by the Deputy Attorney General and place it under the Assistant Attorneys General for the Criminal and National Security Divisions.
quote: The next conservative Administration should direct the Attorney General to remove the FBI from the Deputy Attorney General’s direct supervision

title: Bar the FBI from countering "misinformation"
proposal: The chapter says the FBI should generally be prohibited from working against so-called misinformation and disinformation by Americans not tied to crime, with a firewall against asking platforms to remove content.
quote: Prohibit the FBI from engaging, in general, in activities related to combating the spread of so-called misinformation and disinformation by Americans

title: Eliminate FBI offices such as its General Counsel
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should eliminate any FBI offices it can without Congress, including moving the FBI's roughly 300-lawyer General Counsel office and its own congressional and public affairs offices into main DOJ.
quote: The next conservative Administration should eliminate any offices within the FBI that it has the power to eliminate without any action from Congress.

title: Shrink FBI headquarters and shift resources to field offices
proposal: The chapter says the FBI should reduce headquarters staff and put more funding and rewards into its field offices.
quote: Emphasize, fund, and reward field offices while shrinking headquarters staff.

title: End the FBI Director's 10-year term
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should ask Congress to eliminate the FBI Director's 10-year term so the Director serves like other agency heads.
quote: Submit a legislative proposal to Congress to eliminate the 10-year term for the Director.

title: Require each U.S. Attorney to have a violent crime plan
proposal: The chapter says the Attorney General should require every U.S. Attorney to create a district-specific plan to reduce violent crime and hold them accountable for results.
quote: The Attorney General should require all U.S. Attorneys to develop a jurisdictional-specific plan

title: Bring federal charges where local prosecutors don't
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should use federal law to charge criminals that local jurisdictions let avoid responsibility, and increase federal law enforcement presence in those places.
quote: Use applicable federal laws to bring federal charges against criminals when local jurisdictions wrongfully allow them to evade responsibility for their conduct.

title: Sue local prosecutors who refuse to prosecute crimes
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should, where federal law allows, take legal action against local officials, including District Attorneys, who refuse to prosecute crimes in their areas.
quote: initiate legal action against local officials—including District Attorneys—who deny American citizens the “equal protection of the laws”

title: Seek mandatory minimums for armed career criminals
proposal: The chapter says DOJ prosecutors should consistently pursue mandatory minimum sentences for violent offenders under the Armed Career Criminal Act.
quote: including pursuing mandatory minimum sentences under the Armed Career Criminal Act (ACCA).

title: Back the Restoring the Armed Career Criminal Act
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should support legislation such as the Restoring the Armed Career Criminal Act to strengthen sentencing tools.
quote: The department should also support legislative efforts to provide further tools, such as the Restoring the Armed Career Criminal Act

title: Carry out federal death sentences and seek more
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should do everything possible to carry out sentences for the 44 people on federal death row and seek the death penalty for applicable crimes, especially violent crimes and child sexual abuse.
quote: The next conservative Administration should therefore do everything possible to obtain finality for the 44 prisoners currently on federal death row.

title: Prosecute more interstate drug crimes
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should prosecute as much interstate drug activity as possible, including simple possession of amounts large enough to distribute.
quote: Rigorously prosecute as much interstate drug activity as possible, including simple possession of distributable quantities.

title: Use racketeering (RICO) laws against criminal groups
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should aggressively use the RICO law to prosecute criminal organizations.
quote: Aggressively deploy the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act (RICO),47 which Congress expressly created

title: Finish the southern border wall
proposal: The chapter says the next Administration should finish the wall on the southwestern land border as part of fighting drug cartels.
quote: In addition to finalizing the southwestern land border wall, the next Administration should take a creative and aggressive approach

title: Use active-duty troops and Guard in border arrests
proposal: The chapter says the approach to cartels at the border could include using active-duty military personnel and National Guard members to help with arrest operations.
quote: This could include use of active-duty military personnel and National Guardsmen to assist in arrest operations along the border

title: Restart the DOJ China Initiative
proposal: The chapter says the next Administration should restart the China Initiative, a Trump-era DOJ program focused on Chinese economic espionage and trade secret theft.
quote: Restart the China Initiative.

title: Educate the public on threats from China and Iran
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should pursue other programs to educate Americans about national and economic security threats from foreign actors, especially China and Iran.
quote: Pursue other programs to educate the American people about the real and dangerous threats to our national security and economic security

title: End DOJ policies and cases contrary to Administration policy
proposal: The chapter says before Inauguration Day the next Administration should review DOJ policies, investigations and cases and plan to end immediately those contrary to law or Administration policies.
quote: prepare a plan to end immediately any policies, investigations, or cases that run contrary to law or Administration policies.

title: Review FACE Act prosecutions of pro-life activists
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should end what it calls double standards in FACE Act prosecutions of pro-life activists as part of a wider review of all DOJ activities.
quote: Ensure that its review extends beyond ending the absurd double standards embodied in the ongoing campaign of FACE Act prosecutions

title: End outdated federal consent decrees
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should review all consent decrees and settlement agreements, seek to end unnecessary or outdated ones, and consider intervening in long-running ones.
quote: Seek to terminate any unnecessary or outdated consent decree to which the United States is a party.

title: Ban settlement payments to third parties
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should adopt policies and rules prohibiting settlement payments to third parties.
quote: Enact policies and regulations that prohibit settlement payments to third parties.

title: Align DOJ litigation with the President's agenda
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should issue guidance that litigation decisions must be consistent with the President's agenda and the rule of law, and be ready to discipline attorneys who do not follow it.
quote: Issue guidance to ensure that litigation decisions are consistent with the President’ s agenda and the rule of law.

title: Argue Humphrey's Executor is unconstitutional
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should formally take the position that the Supreme Court case Humphrey's Executor, which allows independent agencies whose heads the President cannot freely fire, violates the Constitution, and potentially seek its overruling.
quote: should formally take the position that Humphrey's Executor violates the Constitution's separation of powers.

title: Lead a government-wide effort against DEI-based discrimination
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should lead all federal agencies in a recommitment to nondiscrimination, working against what it calls unlawful diversity, equity and inclusion programs, including enforcing federal contractor rules.
quote: Ensure that the DOJ spearheads an initiative demonstrating the federal government’ s commitment to nondiscrimination.

title: Use Civil Rights Division to prosecute DEI discrimination
proposal: The chapter says the Civil Rights Division should be reorganized and spend its first year investigating and prosecuting governments, colleges, corporations and employers it finds engaged in illegal discrimination.
quote: using the full force of federal prosecutorial resources to investigate and prosecute all state and local governments, institutions of higher education, corporations

title: Enforce Comstock Act against mailing abortion pills
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should announce it will enforce federal laws (18 U.S.C. 1461 and 1462) against providers and distributors who mail abortion pills.
quote: The Department of Justice in the next conservative Administration should therefore announce its intent to enforce federal law against providers and distributors of such pills.

title: Move election crime prosecutions to the Criminal Division
proposal: The chapter says the Attorney General should move responsibility for prosecuting conspiracy-against-rights election cases (18 U.S.C. 241) from the Civil Rights Division to the Criminal Division.
quote: the Civil Rights Division to the Criminal Division where it belongs. Otherwise, voter registration fraud and unlawful ballot correction will remain

title: Investigate Pennsylvania election guidance from 2020
proposal: The chapter says Pennsylvania's Secretary of State should be investigated and prosecuted for possible violations of 18 U.S.C. 241 over 2020 ballot guidance.
quote: the Pennsylvania Secretary of State should have been (and still should be) investigated and prosecuted for potential violations of 18 U.S. Code § 241.

title: Reject outside groups' requests for political investigations
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should reject demands from outside groups to threaten politically motivated investigations or prosecutions of lawful activity.
quote: The DOJ should reject demands from third-party groups that ask it to threaten politically motivated investigation or prosecution

title: Review all DOJ grant payments
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should immediately review all DOJ grant payments to make sure programs are run properly and recipients use money properly.
quote: Conduct an immediate, comprehensive review of all federal grant disbursals

title: Tighten vetting of DOJ grant applicants
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should overhaul its grant application process with stricter vetting so money goes only to groups that support federal law enforcement; it points to past conditions that blocked "sanctuary city" grants.
quote: Order an overhaul of the DOJ grant application process, to include more rigorous vetting of state, local, and private grant applicants

title: Prioritize prosecution of immigration crimes
proposal: The chapter says the Attorney General should tell all U.S. Attorneys to emphasize prosecuting immigration and immigration-related offenses.
quote: Issue guidance to all U.S. Attorneys emphasizing the importance of prosecuting immigration offenses

title: Help DHS get data on criminal immigrants in sanctuary areas
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should help DHS obtain information about criminal immigrants, especially in "sanctuary" jurisdictions.
quote: Pursue appropriate steps to assist the Department of Homeland Security in obtaining information about criminal aliens in jurisdictions across the United States

title: Reconsider Garland-era immigration decisions
proposal: The chapter says the Attorney General should consider withdrawing or overturning every immigration decision issued by Attorney General Garland and use the power to decide immigration cases directly.
quote: Examine and consider the appropriateness of withdrawing or overturning every immigration decision rendered by Attorney General Garland

title: Reissue every Trump-era immigration court rule
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should, at minimum, reissue through rulemaking every immigration rule from the Trump Administration, such as rules on case delays and asylum eligibility, and write new ones as needed.
quote: pursue through rulemaking—and in partnership with the Department of Homeland Security where appropriate—the promulgation of every rule related to immigration that was issued during the Trump Administration.

title: Put more resources into immigration courts
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should commit enough resources to decide immigration cases in different settings, such as under the Migrant Protection Protocols ("Remain in Mexico").
quote: Commit sufficient resources to the adjudication of cases in the immigration court system in different environments

title: Litigate to overturn the Flores agreement
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should bring lawsuits to undo court precedents that limit immigration powers, such as the Flores Settlement Agreement on detaining migrant children.
quote: by pursuing the overturning of the Flores Settlement Agreement

title: Protect U.S. workers from being passed over for foreign workers
proposal: The chapter says the Civil Rights Division's Immigrant and Employee Rights Section should aggressively make sure no U.S. citizen faces job discrimination in favor of a temporary or foreign worker.
quote: to ensure that no American citizen is discriminated against in the employment context in favor of a temporary or foreign worker.

title: Strengthen anti-fraud efforts in immigration courts
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should run a more vigorous anti-fraud program in the immigration court system, focused on attorney fraud.
quote: Pursue a more vigorous anti-fraud program within the EOIR.

title: Greatly expand political appointees across DOJ
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should seek resources for a large increase in political appointees in every DOJ office, especially the Civil Rights Division, FBI and immigration courts, who are committed to its priorities.
quote: The next conservative Administration must make every effort to obtain the resources to support a vast expansion of the number of appointees in every office and component

title: Recall DOJ staff on detail, including to Congress
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should end and recall all nonessential staff details, especially to congressional offices, until it reviews its personnel needs.
quote: the next conservative Administration should terminate and recall all details of DOJ personnel shortly after the President’s inauguration.

title: Review recent DOJ misconduct findings
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should review all sanctions and misconduct findings from the previous four years to check that they were handled properly.
quote: should complete a thorough review of any sanctions or findings of misconduct issued over the four years preceding the inauguration

title: Review DOJ hiring practices
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should review hiring across all offices to make sure career hires are based on merit and not ideology, group membership, race, religion or sex.
quote: Undertake a comprehensive review of DOJ hiring practices.

title: Consolidate duplicate DOJ support offices
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should explore combining duplicate functions such as human resources, legal counsel, public relations and IT across its components.
quote: should explore the possibility of consolidating and aligning the functions of the DOJ’s various components and offices in human resources, legal counsel, public relations

title: Make division press officers political appointees
proposal: The chapter suggests replacing career public information officers in DOJ divisions with political appointees supervised by the Director of Public Affairs.
quote: This could be made more efficient by having political appointees for each division under the supervision of the Direc-tor of Public Affairs.

title: Merge DOJ legislative and public affairs offices
proposal: The chapter says DOJ's Office of Legislative Affairs and Office of Public Affairs should be combined into one Office of Public and Legislative Affairs.
quote: the two offices should be folded into one for more efficiency and proper coordination.

title: Raise pay for field federal prosecutors
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should ask Congress to reform pay for Assistant U.S. Attorneys in the field, at least matching DOJ headquarters lawyers on the GS scale.
quote: the next conservative Administration should seek congressional reform of the pay scale used for Assistant United States Attorneys in the field.

title: Refocus Bureau of Justice Statistics on core crime data
proposal: The chapter says the Bureau of Justice Statistics should focus on clear core statistics like serious crime, imprisonment and recidivism, and not publish contractor reports that look official. It says NIJ research should follow similar principles.
quote: The BJS should focus on the core statistics involving crime and punishment, such as those relating to serious crimes committed, imprisonment, time served, recidivism

title: Prioritize funding for the National Crime Victimization Survey
proposal: The chapter says DOJ should prioritize and fully fund the National Crime Victimization Survey.
quote: (it dates to the Nixon Administration), is of particular importance, and the department should prioritize and sufficiently fund it.
